overall: Both sets are well made and close to the official format in 8.0: five questions in the official order (word meaning and purpose first, cross-document in the middle and later, the last question on the final document only); three documents of 399 and 495 words (inside 380-560); e-mail, web page, invoice, itinerary and review all have the expected header fields. Consistency checks pass: weekdays match 2025 (March 20 Thursday, March 22 Saturday, June 14 Saturday, June 12 Thursday); the invoice arithmetic is right (34 x 26 = 884; 884 + 35 + 60 - 195 = 784; the deposit is 25 percent of 30 x 26 = 195, received March 4, the day after the e-mail says it will be paid); the lunch and return times (+45 minutes each) agree; the review's complaints (late departure, late lunch, back after six) agree with the e-mail. No second defensible option in any of the 10 questions. Difficulty is above the usual real triple passage: 5 hard, 4 medium, 1 easy by 8.3; a typical real set has one cross-document inference, while 04 has three in a row (Q3-Q5) and 05 has two. The best items are 04:2 and 05:3 (cross-document chains with a believable corrected-information trap). The documents read like business writing (a small amount of British flavor: 'Water' for a lake, 'wedges'), and distractors are mostly of the kind in 8.2 (corrected information, adjacent facts, most common word sense). Weaknesses are small: the two word-meaning items have a couple of weak distractors, the one easy item is at the batch ceiling, and the invoice lacks an event date.
